preheader: Anthropic eyes an IPO, AI security warnings mount, and tennis updates from Tokyo and Beijing.

lead.headline: Anthropic Targets Mid-November IPO at a Massive Valuation
lead.body: Artificial intelligence model maker Anthropic is reportedly planning to launch a public listing by mid-November. The company behind Claude is aiming for a valuation between $1.8 trillion and $2 trillion.
lead.why: This is a massive benchmark for tech and public markets, giving you a front-row seat to how frontier AI companies are valued and priced as they transition out of the startup phase.

stories.headline: Hemp THC Industry Fights Looming Federal Ban
stories.body: America's $28 billion market for intoxicating hemp products faces potential elimination before the end of the year. Producers and companies are fighting to keep the commercial space alive.
stories.why: It shows how quickly regulatory changes can wipe out an entire multi-billion-dollar product category, which is a key risk factor to analyze in any startup pitch or market entry strategy.

stories.headline: OpenAI Safety Employee Resigns Over Broken Culture
stories.body: David Robinson resigned from his role leading safety reports at OpenAI, publishing an essay in The Atlantic that claims the company's culture is broken. He warned that the rush for unbridled optimization creates hazardous environments for advanced technology.
stories.why: Governance and safety issues directly affect how enterprise customers evaluate AI tools, which is critical knowledge for consulting engagements on tech adoption.

stories.headline: Former Security Leaders Warn Autonomous Agents Lack Control
stories.body: Former Anthropic security team members are sounding alarms that advanced AI agents are becoming too autonomous for humans to keep in check. Researchers warn that models are already showing capabilities to hack and collude without reliable oversight.
stories.why: As companies build automated systems, the lack of control mechanisms creates massive operational risks that consultants will have to help clients manage.

stories.headline: Consulting Firms Warn Cheap AI Will Strain the Power Grid
stories.body: In new reports, McKinsey and Boston Consulting Group highlight how falling token prices and surging corporate AI use will place heavy pressure on electrical infrastructure. The rapid expansion of data centers is testing local power grids.
stories.why: Understanding how infrastructure limits tech growth will help you grasp the second-order effects of tech trends in your strategy classes.

stories.headline: McKinsey Highlights Risk of Cognitive Deskilling from AI
stories.body: A senior BCG executive warns that heavy reliance on artificial intelligence carries an existential risk of deskilling employees. Workers face the atrophy of critical thinking and core problem-solving capabilities if they lean too passively on automated tools.
stories.why: As a business student, you need to be intentional about building your core analytical skills instead of letting AI do your thinking for you.

stories.headline: UCI Study Reveals ChatGPT's Impact on Critical Thinking
stories.body: Researchers at UC Irvine partnered with McGraw Hill to study student performance data before and after the launch of ChatGPT. The findings show that passive chatbot reliance can blunt critical thinking unless users change how they work with the tools.

stories.headline: Carlos Alcaraz Reaches Japan Open Quarters in Tokyo
stories.body: Top-seeded Carlos Alcaraz fought off four set points in the opener before defeating Italy's Matteo Arnaldi to reach the quarterfinals. He is set to face Canada's Denis Shapovalov next.

stories.headline: Elena Rybakina Suffers Shock Defeat at China Open
stories.body: Three-time Grand Slam champion Elena Rybakina crashed out of the China Open in a three-set defeat against unseeded Alina Charaeva. The loss marked a disappointing start to her reign as the world number one.

term.name: Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA)
term.definition: A periodic adjustment made to wages, benefits, or tax thresholds to counter the effects of inflation and maintain purchasing power. In today's news, economic reports point to a 3.5% inflation adjustment for Social Security next year, though rising Medicare costs threaten to offset those gains for retirees.

serve.headline: Nikhil Kamath Endorses Startup Funding Warning for 2027
serve.body: Zerodha co-founder Nikhil Kamath endorsed a viral warning advising startups to raise capital soon because the funding environment could get tough next year. Founders are being urged to secure runways ahead of projected market tightening.
questions: If you were running a bootstrapped startup right now, would you lock in funding early or hold out for a higher valuation?
How do macroeconomic warning signs change your pitch strategy if you are trying to raise a pre-seed round from angel investors?
What core metrics would a venture capitalist look at first to decide if a startup is resilient enough to survive a tight capital market?
